case.case_title: Wijeratne v. Vijitha Perera, Sub-Inspector of Police, Polonnaruwa and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, SC Application No. 379/93, decided on 10 January 1994

clause.text: No person shall be arrested except according to law and must be informed of the reason.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was lawfully arrested and informed of the reason for arrest in accordance with Article 13(1).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed he was arrested unlawfully without being given any reason and was detained by the police with the approval of the 2nd respondent.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents denied arrest and detention, claiming the petitioner came voluntarily to the police station and was warned but not arrested.
key_facts: The petitioner was detained overnight at the police station after police searched his house without a warrant or consent.
The petitioner was not given any reason for the search or arrest.
The respondents did not deny the arrest allegation in the complaint letter to the IGP.
The petitioner was a trade union leader involved in peaceful picketing activities.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that Article 13(1) requires lawful arrest and informing the person of the reason. The petitioner was not given any lawful reason or authority for arrest or detention.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The police searched the petitioner’s house without a warrant or consent, seized posters unlawfully, and detained the petitioner overnight without lawful justification or informing him of the reason, thus violating Article 13(1).
principles_established: Arrest must be according to law and the person must be informed of the reason.
Unlawful search and detention violate Article 13(1).
precedents_cited: Mohamed Faiz v. The Attorney-General and Six Others

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner’s fundamental rights under Article 13(1) were infringed by the unlawful arrest and detention.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Compensation awarded to the petitioner; directions issued to police to respect fundamental rights.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(1) was central to the court’s finding that the petitioner was unlawfully arrested and detained without being informed of the reason, leading to a violation of his fundamental rights.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner was not given any reason for the search or arrest; the respondents did not deny the arrest allegation; the police detained the petitioner overnight without lawful authority.
